title: Benchmark run manifest
description: What produced a set of measurements. Every field is here because omitting it makes the numbers mean something other than they appear to.

suite.description: Suite name, matching a file in benchmarks/suites/.

started_at.description: UTC, ISO-8601. Also the run directory's name.

dirty.description: Uncommitted changes present. A dirty run is not reproducible from the sha, so it must not be published as a baseline.

machine.description: Latency is largely a property of the host, so comparing across machines needs this stated.

embedder.description: Read from the palace, not from configuration: what matters is the embedder the index was built with. Configuration can disagree with it, and did once — a quality benchmark measured minilm while production ran embeddinggemma.

embedder_source.description: Where the embedder value came from. 'configured' is weaker evidence and should be treated as provisional.

split.description: A number from the split used for tuning is not a number about generalisation. Held-out results are the publishable ones.

metric.description: Retrieval recall and end-to-end accuracy are different measurements. Reporting them side by side without this label is how benchmark tables mislead.

scale.description: How much was stored. Recall latency grows with it, so a latency figure without it is incomparable.

command.description: The exact invocation, so the run can be repeated.

notes.description: Anything that qualifies the numbers — a warm cache, a busy machine, a known-broken subsystem.
